A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 42-page ST-WebAgentBench paper, including Appendices A–I. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison establish complete comparability; differences are confined to administrative metadata and the first-page arXiv stamp.

before.justification: v6 reports original three-agent evaluations in Section 4 and Figure 2, dimension ablations in Table 3, and policy-load results in Appendix C.

after.justification: v7 retains the original three-agent evaluations, dimension ablations, and policy-load results in Section 4, Table 3, and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The policy hierarchy, evaluator templates, POLICY_CONTEXT injection, and human-in-the-loop mechanism are identical. Appendix I's proposed policy-controller architecture is also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same 375 tasks across GitLab, ShoppingAdmin, and SuiteCRM, including difficulty tiers and 80 Modality Challenge tasks (Section 3 and Table 2). No coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Section 4 and Figure 2 evaluate the same agents: AWM, WebVoyager, and WorkArena-Legacy. No comparator is added, removed, or revised within any reported comparison.

E3.justification: The reported GPT-4o backbone, pass@3 evaluation, task allocations, scoring metrics, and simulated user confirmation are unchanged. Appendix C retains the same policy-load bins and analysis procedure.

E4.justification: The dimension-removal ablation in Table 3, policy-load analysis in Appendix C, and agent-failure case studies in Appendices D and H are identical.

E5.justification: Repeated-attempt reporting, pass@3/all-pass@3 practices, and statistical uncertainty reporting are unchanged. Appendix C retains the same significance reporting, slope uncertainty, and statement that standard-error bars are omitted.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results match. For example, Figure 2 reports CuP of 20%, 10.3%, and 15% for AWM, WebVoyager, and WorkArena respectively in both versions; Table 3 and Appendix C results also match.

T1.justification: The policy hierarchy and admissible-action formulation in Section 3.1, metric definitions in Section 3.3, and threat-model assumptions in Appendix G.1 are identical. No mathematical reasoning or proof is added or corrected.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical contributions and claims concerning the policy-aware benchmark, safety-aware metrics, and gap between nominal completion and policy-compliant performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations of consent failures, hallucination, and policy-load degradation are unchanged. The same limitations concerning agent selection, English-language enterprise coverage, expert-panel context, and excluded threats remain in Section 5 and the appendices.

D1.justification: Hardware, runtime, hosting, policy templates, prompts, evaluator code, and reproduction instructions are identical (Section 4.1 and Appendices D–H). The code and dataset access links also have unchanged targets.

R1.justification: Section 2, the benchmark-positioning comparison in Table 1, and the reference list are identical. No cited work or substantive relationship to prior research changes.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v6 dated 2 March 2026 to v7 dated 4 June 2026. PDF author metadata adds Nir Mashkif, already present in both printed bylines; the prose, headings, and section order are unchanged.

P2.justification: The updated first-page arXiv margin stamp is slightly recentered. Figures 1–17, Tables 1–19, captions, and all other layout remain unchanged; pages 2–42 render pixel-identically.

improvement.justification: v7 makes administrative updates to the version/date stamp and author metadata. The scientific text, evidence, appendices, reproducibility information, and substantive presentation are unchanged, establishing no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
